statements.claim: Bhishma, at the head of the Kaurava host, cased in mail and bow in hand, showered arrows on Abhimanyu, Arjuna, the ruler of the Kekayas, Virata, Dhrishtadyumna of Prishata's race, and the Chedi and Matsya warriors.
statements.evidence: Pack passage MBh 6.52 (Ganguli): Bhishma 'showered an arrowy downpour on the heroic son of Subhadra, and the mighty car-warrior Arjuna, and the ruler of the Kekayas and Virata, and Dhrishtadyumna of Prishata's race, as also upon the Chedi and the Matsya warriors.'

statements.claim: The Pandava array wavered at Bhishma's onset; horsemen, car-warriors and foremost steeds fell fast, and the car-divisions of the Pandavas began to fly away.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.52: 'that mighty array (of the Pandavas) wavered at the onset of that hero... horse-men and car-warriors and foremost of steeds fell fast. And the car-divisions of the Pandavas began to fly away.'

statements.claim: Arjuna angrily asked Krishna to proceed to the grandsire, saying Bhishma with wrath excited would annihilate his host for Duryodhana's benefit, and that Drona, Kripa, Salya and Vikarna with Dhritarashtra's sons would slaughter the Panchalas, so he himself would slay Bhishma.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.52 (near-verbatim): 'Proceed to the place where the grandsire is... this Bhishma, with wrath excited, will annihilate for Duryodhana's benefit my host... will slaughter the Panchalas. Even I, therefore, shall slay Bhishma for the sake of my troops.'

statements.claim: Krishna answered: 'Be careful, O Dhananjaya, for I will soon take thee, O hero, towards the grandsire's car.'
statements.evidence: MBh 6.52 (verbatim); also pack excerpt.

statements.claim: The car Krishna drove was celebrated over the world, with numerous waving banners, steeds handsome as a flight of white cranes, a roaring ape on its standard, of solar effulgence with a rattle like the roar of clouds, and he drove it before Bhishma's car through the Kaurava divisions and the Surasenas.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.52: Saurin 'took that car, which was celebrated over the world, before the car of Bhishma... slaughtering the Kaurava divisions and the Surasenas also.' Car description matches verbatim.

statements.claim: Bhishma, protected by warriors headed by Saindhava and by the combatants of the East, the Sauviras and the Kekayas, met Arjuna with great impetuosity.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.52 passage.

statements.claim: Bhishma struck Vasudeva himself between his two breasts with three arrows, and the charioteer took the shafts without flinching and held the car steady.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Bhishma, that foremost of smiters, struck Vasudeva between his two breasts with three arrows.' The 'did not flinch / held the car steady' line is unobjectionable connective on top of that event.

statements.claim: In the duel Arjuna was pierced by Bhishma with seventy-seven arrows, Drona with twenty-five, Kripa with fifty, Duryodhana with sixty-four, Salya with nine, Drona's son with sixty, Vikarna with three, Saindhava with nine, Sakuni with five, and Artayani with three broad-headed arrows.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.52 passage lists exactly these numbers for the same named warriors.

statements.claim: Pierced on all sides, Arjuna wavered not like a mountain pierced with arrows, and in return pierced Bhishma with twenty-five, Kripa with nine, Drona with sixty, Vikarna with three, Artayani with three and Duryodhana with five arrows.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.52: 'that great bowman... wavered not like a mountain that is pierced (with arrows)... pierced Bhishma with five and twenty, and Kripa with nine arrows, and Drona with sixty... Vikarna with three arrows; and Artayani with three arrows, and the king (Duryodhana) also with five.'

statements.claim: Satyaki, Virata, Dhrishtadyumna, the sons of Draupadi and Abhimanyu surrounded Arjuna in support, while the prince of the Panchalas advanced against Drona.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.52 passage.

statements.claim: Bhishma pierced Arjuna with eighty sharp arrows, gratifying the combatants on Duryodhana's side; Arjuna then cheerfully sported with his bow among the mighty car-warriors, and king Duryodhana, seeing his troops afflicted, spoke to Bhishma.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.52 passage.

statements.claim: The closing question — who else save the Kuru grandsire, Drona and Karna could advance against the bearer of Gandiva — hung over the field.
statements.evidence: The rhetorical line appears in MBh 6.52 ('Who else save the Kuru grandsire and those car-warriors, viz., Drona and Vikartana's son (Karna), are capable of advancing...?'); the story's loose framing of it is atmosphere, not a new factual assertion.

notes: All narrative details track the pack's MBh 6.52 passage nearly verbatim; story ends with the three arrows in Krishna's breast, consistent with the canonical event.

statements.claim: The Pandavas had won the forenoon of the day when Bhishma, bound by the dreadful vow he had sworn at Duryodhana's words, rushed with his fleetest steeds at the Pandava army, protected by a large force and by all of Dhritarashtra's sons.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59 (pack passage): 'After the forenoon of that day... had passed away... and after the high-souled Pandavas had won the victory, thy sire Devavrata... rushed carried by the fleetest steeds, towards the army of the Pandavas, protected by a large force and by all thy sons.' Dhritarashtra's framing question confirms the 'dreadful vow... by Bhishma enraged by the words of my son.'

statements.claim: The battle's uproar (twang of bows like splitting hills, 'Stay—Here I stand—Strike' cries), the falling of gold coats of mail, crowns, diadems and standards like stones on stony ground, and heads and arms falling by hundreds and thousands.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59 passage.

statements.claim: A dreadful river of blood flowed, impetuous, miry with flesh and blood, with dead elephants for its rocks, running toward the ocean of the next world and delightful to vultures and jackals; cars could not make their way for the slain; some wounded rushed cheerfully on the foe; others cried to father, brother, friend and kinsman not to abandon them.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59 passage (verbatim imagery).

statements.claim: Bhishma, with bow drawn into a circle, shot shafts of blazing points like snakes of virulent poison, smote Pandava car-warriors naming each beforehand, and seemed to be everywhere at once like a circle of fire, seen east then west, multiplied a thousand-fold, so that all regarded him as multiplied by illusion; none of the Pandavas could even look at him.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59 passage.

statements.claim: Kings in thousands fell upon Bhishma like senseless insects on a fire; with one straight shaft he despatched a single elephant like a hill riven by the thunderbolt; he pierced two or three elephant-riders at a time with one arrow; whoever approached him, seen for a moment, was next beheld to fall.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59 passage.

statements.claim: The vast host of Yudhishthira the just gave way in a thousand directions, trembling in the very presence of Vasudeva and the high-souled Partha.
statements.evidence: MBh 6.59 passage.

statements.claim: Opening hook: 'Krishna stepped down from the chariot in the middle of a battle, and no arrow had touched him.'
statements.evidence: The pack passage is truncated at the crucial point, but the authoritative Ganguli 6.59 text it is drawn from states that shortly before Krishna descended, Bhishma 'pierced both Vasudeva and Dhananjaya with keen shafts all over their bodies... covered the two Krishnas on all sides with shafts in hundreds and thousands. And with those keen shafts of his, the enraged Bhishma caused him of Vrishni's race to shiver.' The corpus's own immediately preceding canonical event (DKS_0464 / MBh 6.52) likewise has Bhishma strike Vasudeva between the breasts with three arrows the same day. 'No arrow had touched him' therefore contradicts the source account.

statements.claim: Krishna, his wrath kindled at seeing the host of his friends reaped, rose and stepped down from the car, making to end it himself and striding toward the grandsire.
statements.evidence: Pack summary ('Arjuna seizes the enraged Krishna and stops him at the tenth step') and Ganguli 6.59: Krishna, unable to bear Bhishma's slaughter of Yudhishthira's host, resolves 'Accoutred in mail, even I will stay Bhishma to-day for the sake of the Pandavas' and, abandoning the reins, jumps down from the car. 'No one had ever seen the charioteer leave his car' is connective emphasis.

statements.claim: Arjuna jumped down from his own car and ran on foot after Krishna, his long arms outstretched, seized him by his two hands, and stopped him with difficulty at the tenth step.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'jumping down from his car, Partha... quickly ran on foot after that chief of Yadu's race... seized him by his two hands... succeeded... in stopping him with difficulty at the tenth step.'

statements.claim: Arjuna said: 'Quell this wrath of thine. Thou art the refuge of the Pandavas, O Krishna. I swear to thee that I will not withdraw from the acts to which I have pledged myself.'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (verbatim; source addresses 'O Kesava', same referent).

statements.claim: Gratified by the promise, Krishna returned to the chariot, gathered the reins, and sounded the conch Panchajanya, the blast carrying across the field.
statements.evidence: Pack summary ('Krishna is gratified, returns to the chariot, and sounds the Panchajanya') and Ganguli 6.59: 'Janardana became gratified... once more... mounted on his car... once more took up those reins... and taking up his conch called Panchajanya, Saurin filled all the points of the compass... with its blare.' The 'told both armies the war would go on' gloss is connective.

corrections.original_sentence: Krishna stepped down from the chariot in the middle of a battle, and no arrow had touched him.
corrections.suggested: Krishna stepped down from the chariot in the middle of a battle, though the grandsire's shafts had already struck him that day.

notes: One real error: the hook claims Krishna was untouched by arrows, but Ganguli 6.59 (the pack's own source; the pack passage truncates just before these lines) has Bhishma pierce both Vasudeva and Arjuna with shafts and make Krishna shiver before he descends, and the prior canonical event (6.52, DKS_0464) has three arrows strike Krishna between the breasts. Everything else tracks the passage closely.

statements.claim: After the ruler of the Sindhus (Jayadratha) had been slain by Arjuna, Kripa son of Saradwat, enraged, covered Arjuna with a dense shower of arrows, and Drona's son rushed against him from his car; the two poured keen arrows on Arjuna from opposite directions, and he, afflicted, felt great pain.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.146 (pack passage, verbatim).

statements.claim: Arjuna did not desire to slay his preceptor Kripa (who had taught him the science of arms) or Drona's son, so he baffled their weapons and sped mildly-coursing shafts not meant to kill, though their number caused great pain; Kripa swooned on the terrace of his car and his driver, believing him dead, bore him away; Drona's son fled from fear.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.146 passage: 'Without desiring, however, to slay his preceptor (Kripa) as also the son of (his other preceptor) Drona... he sped at them... shafts that coursed mildly... Kripa... swooned away on the terrace of his car... the driver... bore Kripa away... Aswatthaman also, from fear, fled away.' Kripa as teacher of arms is confirmed by Arjuna's own lament in the same passage.

statements.claim: Arjuna lamented on his car with a tearful face, recalling Vidura's words at Suyodhana's birth that owing to him a great calamity would overtake the foremost of Kuru's race; he said Kripa, a rishi's son, his preceptor and Drona's dear friend, lay on a bed of arrows because of him, and that striking a preceptor leads to hell, and he had disobeyed Kripa's command never to strike his preceptor.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.146 passage (near-verbatim rendering of the lament, including the quoted Vidura prophecy and Kripa's command).

statements.claim: While Arjuna was lamenting, Karna, beholding the ruler of the Sindhus slain, rushed toward him; the two Panchala princes and Satyaki suddenly rushed at Karna.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.146 passage.

statements.claim: Arjuna asked Krishna to urge the steeds toward where Karna came, saying Karna was unable to bear the slaughter of Bhurisravas and must not be allowed to make Satyaki follow in Bhurisravas's wake.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.146 passage (near-verbatim).

statements.claim: Krishna held Arjuna back in opportune words: the mighty-armed Satyaki is singly a match for Karna, and more so when united with the two sons of Drupada; it was not proper for Arjuna to fight Karna then, since Karna had the blazing dart, like a fierce meteor, that Vasava (Indra) gave him, and had kept it for Arjuna.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt from MBh 7.146 (verbatim through 'he hath kept it for t...'; completed by the passage's own text 'kept it for thee').

statements.claim: Karna swept past toward Satyaki and the Panchalas with the blazing dart still unspent in his keeping.
statements.evidence: The claim that Karna carried the dart 'across the war, through every battle, spending nothing' extends Krishna's statement that the dart 'hath been kept for thee'; it is narrative elaboration of the same idea, not a new verifiable event.

notes: Long dialogue passages track the pack's MBh 7.146 passage almost verbatim (Kripa/Ashvatthama duel, Arjuna's lament, dart speech). No factual issues.

statements.claim: Recap: after Jayadratha's death Karna, unable to bear the slaughter of Bhurisravas, rushed toward Arjuna; Satyaki with the two Panchala princes rushed to meet him; Arjuna wanted to drive into the fight but Krishna held him back, speaking of the blazing dart Karna kept for him.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.146 (pack passage) as in DKS_0466; the corpus chain continues from that event.

statements.claim: Before the encounter Krishna knew in his heart that the heroic Satyaki would be vanquished, for Janardana knows both the past and the future.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (MBh 7.146): 'Before even the encounter, Krishna knew it in his heart that the heroic Satyaki would be vanquished... Janardana, O king, knoweth both the past and the future.'

statements.claim: Krishna summoned his charioteer Daruka and commanded him: 'Let my car be kept equipped tomorrow.'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (MBh 7.146): 'summoning his charioteer, Daruka, he had commanded him, saying, "Let my car be kept equipped tomorrow."' (Ganguli adds that the command preceded the encounter, matching the story's 'beforehand' framing.)

statements.claim: Krishna blew his conch to summon the car at the moment of need, and Daruka brought Krishna's car, which resembled the blazing fire or the sun in effulgence; with Kesava's permission Satyaki ascended it.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'With Kesava's permission, upon that car guided by Daruka, and which resembled the blazing fire or the sun in effulgence...' Ganguli 7.146 (Section CXLVI) confirms the conch: 'Beholding Satyaki carless and Karna ready for battle Madhava blew his conch... Daruka, hearing the blare... soon took that car... to where Kesava was.'

statements.claim: Satyaki's fight against Karna went against him: the Satwata hero was pressed and vanquished, his own car unable to save him.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt states Krishna foresaw 'that the heroic Satyaki would be vanquished,' and Ganguli 7.146 shows Satyaki 'carless' at the moment Krishna sent the car and 'ground... with arrowy downpours' by Karna before being rescued by the arrival of Krishna's car. (The pack passage is truncated before this point; full section confirms the carless state.)

statements.claim: Satyaki, upon the blazing car guided by Daruka, turned again toward Karna, who now faced the car of the charioteer of the Pandavas.
statements.evidence: Ganguli 7.146: after ascending, 'Satyaki rushed against the son of Radha, scattering countless shafts.'

statements.claim: Reflective framing: Krishna lent his own celebrated car, with his own driver, to a warrior who was not one of the five brothers, having prepared for the moment beforehand.
statements.evidence: Commentary on the supported facts of the car-lending (foreknowledge, command to Daruka, permission to mount); no new factual assertion requiring separate support.

notes: The story's 'that morning, when Arjuna had wanted to charge into the fight himself' recap loosely dates the earlier dart-speech (pack gives no time of day; the corpus chain places it after Jayadratha's fall); treated as connective. Pack passage is truncated before the car-lending scene, but the pack excerpt plus full Ganguli 7.146 (Section CXLVI) verify every claim, including the conch summon and Satyaki's carless state.

statements.claim: Karna had stripped Bhima of his chariot, and Bhima, standing on the bare ground, told Arjuna that Karna had called him eunuch, fool, glutton and unskilled in weapons in Arjuna's very sight, and reminded Arjuna of the vow he had made jointly with him, urging him to act so that neither vow would be falsified.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.147 (pack passage): 'After Bhimasena had been made carless... Karna hath repeatedly said to me, "Eunuch, fool, glutton, unskilled in weapons..."... thou knowest the vow which I have made jointly with thee...' Arjuna later confirms to Karna: 'It is true thou hadst succeeded in depriving Bhimasena of his car.'

statements.claim: Recap: that day Arjuna had sworn to slay Jayadratha, who had helped bring down Abhimanyu, before sunset; the vow was fulfilled — Jayadratha lay dead and Vriddhakshatra, his father, died with him.
statements.evidence: Krishna's speech in the pack passage: 'thy great vow hath been accomplished... that Vriddhakshatra hath been slain along with his son'; the son-of-Subhadra slaying by Karna 'with others... out of my sight' is asserted by Arjuna in the same passage. (The Jayadratha-vow backstory belongs to the corpus chain's earlier stories and is here a recap.)

statements.claim: Arjuna told Karna he fought falsely and applauded himself; that heroes meet victory or defeat, both uncertain even when Indra himself fights.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.147 passage (near-verbatim).

statements.claim: Arjuna said: 'When Yuyudhana made you carless, your senses left you and you stood at the very point of death. I remembered my vow to slay you, and I dismissed you without taking your life.'
statements.evidence: Pack passage MBh 7.147: 'Made carless by Yuyudhana, with thy senses no longer under thy control, thou wert almost at the point of death. Remembering, however, that I had vowed to slay thee, that hero dismissed thee without taking thy life.' The merciful dismissal was performed by 'that hero' — Yuyudhana (Satyaki), mindful of Arjuna's vow — not by Arjuna himself, so the story's 'I dismissed you' misattributes the act.

statements.claim: Arjuna said the truly righteous, having vanquished a foe, never boast nor speak ill of anyone; that Karna's abuse of Bhima was sinful; and that since Karna had spoken so harshly of Bhima and had with others slain Abhimanyu out of his sight, Karna would reap the fruit that very day: Arjuna would slay Vrishasena before his eyes and send every king who advanced against him to Yama's abode, and a great calamity hung over Karna.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.147 passage (near-verbatim, including 'I will slay Vrishasena in thy very sight in battle' and 'a great calamity is impending over thee').

statements.claim: A loud and tremendous uproar rose among the car-warriors, and at that frightful time the thousand-rayed sun dimmed its rays and went down behind the Asta hill.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.147 passage: 'the thousand-rayed sun, dimming his rays, entered the Asta hill.'

statements.claim: Krishna, stationed in the van of battle, embraced Arjuna and said his great vow was accomplished, Vriddhakshatra was slain with his son, that even the celestial generalissimo would lose his senses against this host, that no one in the three worlds except Arjuna could fight it, that his energy and might equaled Rudra's or the Destroyer's, and that Krishna would applaud him again in the same words when Karna of wicked soul was slain.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.147 passage (near-verbatim).

statements.claim: Arjuna replied that through Krishna's grace the vow the gods could accomplish only with difficulty had been accomplished, that those who have Krishna for their lord do not wonder at victory, that through his grace Yudhishthira would obtain the whole earth, and that all this was Krishna's power — 'This is your victory, my lord. Our prosperity is your victory.'
statements.evidence: MBh 7.147 passage (near-verbatim: 'This is thy victory, O lord! Our prosperity is thy victory').

corrections.original_sentence: When Yuyudhana made you carless, your senses left you and you stood at the very point of death. I remembered my vow to slay you, and I dismissed you without taking your life.
corrections.suggested: When Yuyudhana made you carless, your senses left you and you stood at the very point of death. Remembering the vow I had made to slay you, that hero dismissed you without taking your life.

notes: One misattribution: the pack passage has Yuyudhana (Satyaki) spare Karna out of regard for Arjuna's vow, while the story's paraphrase puts the dismissal in Arjuna's mouth. All other dialogue tracks the passage near-verbatim.

statements.claim: As the chariot turned back across the field in the failing light after the day's battle, Krishna pointed out the fallen and spoke: 'Desirous of victory in battle, or of world-wide fame, many heroic kings are lying on the earth, struck down by your shafts.'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (MBh 7.147, Ganguli): 'Desirous of victory in battle or world-wide fame many heroic kings are lying on the earth, struck with thy shafts.'

statements.claim: Krishna told Arjuna to behold those huge creatures, afflicted with shafts, lying on the ground in convulsions.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Behold, O hero, those huge creatures afflicted with shafts lying on the ground in convulsions.' (Context and the story's phrasing identify them as the great elephants; the story also shows the horses lying struck among them.)

statements.claim: Krishna said the fame-enhancing and mighty feat on the field of battle was capable of being achieved only by Arjuna.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'This fame-enhancing and mighty feat on the field of battle is capable of being achieved by thee only, O puissant one.'

statements.claim: The setting — sunset, a quiet field covered with the dead of the day's fighting, fallen chariots, a stray horse over its fallen rider, kings of great and small kingdoms lying among elephants and horses — and Arjuna's wordless reflection.
statements.evidence: Atmosphere and reflective framing built around the excerpt's core image of the field strewn with kings and stricken creatures; the 'single day of war' phrasing refers to that day's carnage, not a claim about total war duration.

notes: The pack's prose passage is a duplicate of the MBh 7.147 passage used for DKS_0468 (Bhima-carless episode) and does not itself contain the quoted speech; the pack excerpt is clearly the intended evidence for this event and matches the story's quotations verbatim. Per instructions, the excerpt/summary reading was treated as authoritative.

statements.claim: At night Duryodhana reproached Karna and Drona: the battle had been set on foot by them in rage after the ruler of the Sindhus fell to Arjuna's arrows; they watched the slaughter of his army with indifference though competent to vanquish it; they had told him 'We two shall vanquish the sons of Pandu,' and had they said otherwise he would never have provoked these hostilities.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.172 (pack passage, near-verbatim).

statements.claim: Pierced by the goad of his speech, Karna and Drona went back into battle like snakes vexed with sticks; the Pandavas united and advanced with all their troops.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.172 passage.

statements.claim: Drona pierced Satyaki with ten arrows, Karna with ten more, Duryodhana with seven, Vrishasena with ten and Suvala's son with seven, so that the grandson of Sini stood in an impervious wall of Kauravas.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.172 passage: 'Drona... pierced (Satyaki)... with ten arrows. And Karna pierced him with ten arrows, and thy son with seven, and Vrishasena pierced him with ten, and Suvala's son with seven. In that impervious wall of Kauravas around the grandson of Sini...'

statements.claim: The Somakas pierced Drona from every side with showers of arrows, and Drona, enraged, began taking the lives of Kshatriyas like the sun destroying darkness with his rays.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.172 passage.

statements.claim: A loud uproar rose among the Panchalas; some abandoned sons, fathers, brothers, uncles and kinsmen and fled, some ran senseless at Drona himself; that night the Pandava host fled throwing down blazing torches in the very sight of Bhima, Arjuna, Krishna, the twins, Yudhishthira and Dhrishtadyumna; only the light among the Kaurava troops showed where the fugitives ran; Drona and Karna pursued the flying host scattering shafts.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.172 passage (near-verbatim).

statements.claim: Krishna, becoming cheerless, told Arjuna that Dhrishtadyumna and Satyaki with the Panchalas had gone against Drona and Karna, that the host was broken and routed and could not be rallied, and urged: 'Seeing the host fly away through fear — you Pandava warriors, cast away your fears! With all the forces arrayed in good order, the two of us, with uplifted weapons, are even now proceeding against Drona and the son of the Suta, to withstand them.'
statements.evidence: MBh 7.172 passage and pack excerpt (near-verbatim).

statements.claim: Krishna then pointed out Bhima advancing against Drona and Karna, surrounded by the Somakas and Pandavas, and told Arjuna to fight, supported by Bhima and the many mighty car-warriors, to assure all his troops.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.172 passage (near-verbatim).

statements.claim: Arjuna and Krishna approached Drona and Karna and took their station at the head of battle; the vast force of Yudhishthira saw them and returned to the fight; at dead of night a fierce encounter took place like two oceans swelling at moonrise; the Kaurava warriors threw away their blazing lamps and fought fearlessly and madly under gloom and dust.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.172 passage (near-verbatim).

notes: Rendering tracks MBh 7.172 almost verbatim throughout, including both of Krishna's rallying speeches. Closing line ('Krishna was looking past Drona and Karna... at a time that had not come yet') is foreshadowing connective.

statements.claim: Karna struck Dhrishtadyumna on the chest with ten shafts that pierced to the very vitals, and Dhrishtadyumna pierced him back with five, crying 'Wait! Wait!'; the two shrouded each other with showers of arrows from bows drawn to their fullest stretch.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.173 (pack passage, near-verbatim).

statements.claim: Karna despatched Dhrishtadyumna's driver and four steeds to Yama's abode, cut his foremost bow with keen arrows and felled his driver with a broad-headed shaft; Dhrishtadyumna, deprived of car, steeds and driver, jumped down, took up a mace and, though struck by Karna's straight shafts, approached and slew Karna's four steeds.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.173 passage.

statements.claim: Dhrishtadyumna climbed onto Arjuna's car and would have gone back at Karna, but Yudhishthira bade him desist.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.173 passage: 'quickly ascended the car of Dhananjaya... desired to proceed towards Karna. Dharma's son (Yudhishthira), however, bade him desist.'

statements.claim: Karna mingled leonine shouts with his bow's twang and blew his conch with great force; the Panchalas and Somakas, seeing their prince vanquished, rushed at him making death itself their goal; Karna's driver had yoked fresh steeds, white as conchs, of the Sindhu breed, well-broken and swift, and Karna afflicted the Panchala warriors like a cloud pouring rain on a mountain, so that the Panchala host fled like a doe frightened by a lion.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.173 passage (near-verbatim).

statements.claim: With razor-faced arrows Karna cut off the arms of flying combatants and heads decked with ear-rings, and cut the thighs of men on elephants, horses and the earth; many fled without feeling the loss of their limbs, took the motion of a straw for Karna, and fled from their own friends mistaking them for him; Karna pursued the broken retreating host shooting shafts on all sides.
statements.evidence: MBh 7.173 passage (near-verbatim).

statements.claim: Yudhishthira, beholding his army flying, told Arjuna that Karna stood there like Rudra armed with his bow, scorching everything like the blazing sun at dead of night, that the wails were the cries of their helpless friends mangled by his shafts, that he aimed and loosed with no interval between the acts, and asked Arjuna to do what should next be done about the slaughter of Karna, 'for the time may have come.'
statements.evidence: MBh 7.173 passage (near-verbatim).

statements.claim: Arjuna told Krishna that the son of Dharma was frightened by Karna's prowess, that the army was flying broken and mangled by Drona's shafts and frightened by Karna, that he could not bear seeing Karna careering fearlessly (like a snake that cannot bear the tread of a man), and asked to be taken to Karna: 'I will either kill him — or let him slay me.'
statements.evidence: MBh 7.173 passage (near-verbatim, including the snake simile and 'I will either kill him... or let him slay me').

statements.claim: Krishna held Arjuna back: he beheld Karna careering like the chief of the celestials himself and there was none else who could stand against him, but the time had not come for Arjuna to encounter the son of the Suta, for the blazing dart given by Vasava (Indra) was still with him, still unused; instead Krishna commanded Ghatotkacha, Hidimva's son: 'Slay Karna in battle, at this dead of night.'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (MBh 7.173): 'I behold Karna, O son of Kunti... I do not, however... regard the time to have come... for thee to encounter the Suta's son in battle. The blazing dart... given him by Vasava, is still with him... Let the mighty Ghatotkacha proceed against the son of Radha.' ... 'addressed Hidimva's son... "Slay Karna in battle, at this dead [of night]."' The purpose — that the dart be spent on Ghatotkacha before Arjuna ever meets Karna — is the pack summary's own reading.

notes: Rendering is near-verbatim to the pack's MBh 7.173 passage through Yudhishthira's and Arjuna's speeches and Krishna's reply (the pack passage truncates at 'there is none else'; the excerpt completes Krishna's speech and the command to Ghatotkacha). The 'pierced to the very vitals' phrasing slightly strengthens the source's 'capable of penetrating into the very vitals' — immaterial to the outcome, not flagged.
